# HOLYOKE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND INDUSTRIAL CORPORATION

**Meeting Minutes of August 13, 2026**

**Holyoke City Hall - Room 6**

536 Dwight Street, Holyoke, MA

and via Zoom Meeting ID: 87843442974

**Members Present:** Joseph McGiverin, Catherine Pratt, Antonio Quinones, Michael Sullivan, Carl Eger

**Staff Present:** Eric Nakajima, Executive Director; John Dyjach, Assistant Director

**Others Present:** Keith Crane and Omar Martinez (Engie North America), Shawn Rising (Tighe & Bond), Samantha Curran

## 1. Call to Order

Chairperson Joseph McGiverin noted that alternative access to City Hall was provided due to the ongoing construction. He then called the meeting to order at 5:02 p.m. and stated that the meeting is being held in person, remotely and being recorded. A roll call followed:

| Name | Present |
|---|---|
| Antonio Quinones | Y |
| Catherine Pratt | Y |
| Michael Sullivan | Y |
| Joseph McGiverin | Y |
| Carl Eger | Y |

Chairperson McGiverin said that if there is no objection the agenda will be taken out of order to accommodate our guests.

## 2. Real Estate Project Updates

### a. Economic Development Plan for former Mt. Tom Power Plant Property - discussion with property representatives from Engie North America

Eric Nakajima introduced Keith Crane and Omar Martinez who are here representing Engie North America who is the owner of the former Mt. Tom Power Plant site. He noted that staff has been in dialogue with Mr. Crane for over a year discussing the future opportunities at the site, including HEDIC's interest in developing an Economic Development Plan.

Keith Crane said he visited the site today with Mr. Martinez and others to get a first hand look at the conditions. He said it is important that HEDIC and the City understand that as is the site has ten to possibly fifteen usable acres. He then discussed potential future paths for ownership of the property. These include selling the property outright to an interested third party, selling all or part of the property to a capable entity that would address the environmental conditions to their and regulators satisfaction, and third scenario is to find a way to reduce costs of the site which are primarily real estate taxes and ongoing environmental compliance. He said that status quo is not why they are here but to explore solutions. Mr. Cane added that there is no path defined but they are open to the idea of selling the property to a private entity or a public entity such as HEDIC.

There was then a discussion about the property conditions and limitations. Shawn Rising of Tighe & Bond, which helps to manage the property for Engie, provided a detailed overview of the conditions and answered questions. He noted the limitations as well as ongoing environmental compliance and that there also may be some additional work needed in the near future to stabilize the area around Kennedy Brook.

Joseph McGiverin asked about the future of the Solar Field at the southern end of the property. Mr. Crane said that business operation is handled by another unit at Engie but thinks they would welcome a discussion about it, especially since energy markets are constantly changing and they regularly consider their assets. He added that they have looked at parceling off the solar field but there are challenges with access and egress to the area.

Keith Crane mentioned the need to consider renewing the Memorandum of Understanding between HEDIC and Engie. Chairperson McGiverin agreed and said that is another item on the agenda. He thanked Mr. Crane and Mr. Martinez and appreciates their continuing collaboration with HEDIC to hopefully get to a conclusion that benefits all interests.

### b. Memorandum of Understanding with Mt. Tom Generating Co., LLC (possible vote on first amendment)

The Board considered the amendment to the MOU between HEDIC and Engie. John Dyjach noted that it was a six month agreement that just recently expired. He described the MOU as a document that formally defines a working relationship and that the amendment extends the agreement with no set expiration date. He noted that it was reviewed by Atty. Bissonnette but still needed Engie's final legal review. Chairperson McGiverin said that he agrees with the extension but that any future transaction on the property with Engie would require an Economic Development Plan supported by the Mayor and City Council. Eric Nakajima suggested that the Board consider next steps with Engie at the next Board meeting.

A motion was made by Carl Eger and seconded by Michale Sullivan to extend the MOU with Mt.Tom Generating Co., LLC. as stated, and with the same terms as already agreed to. A roll call followed:

| Name | Yes |
|---|---|
| Catherine Pratt | Y |
| Antonio Quinones | Y |
| Michael Sullivan | Y |
| Carl Eger | Y |
| Joseph McGiverin | Y |

## 3. Board Business

### a. Minutes of June 25, 2026

The meeting minutes of June 25, 2026 were tabled due to a lack of a quorum of members present at that meeting.

## 4. Executive Meeting (if necessary)

No Executive meeting necessary.

## 5. Ongoing and Other Business

### a. Possible Grant Opportunity

John Dyjach explained that staff is exploring the availability of any remaining funds from a grant issued about ten years ago as a result of the Mt. Tom Power Plant closure. He explained the funds are restricted to a renewable energy project and that previously some of those funds were used with the HG&E and to support the efforts of the Redevelopment Authority for the Parsons Paper Redevelopment Project. Michael Sullivan noted one potential project for these funds is to address the conditions at the former Gas Works property that is near the Holyoke Dam. John Dyjach said this is exploratory at this time but if the funds are available there may be a project that involves HEDIC's participation.

Chairperson McGiverin asked Samantha Curran who had joined the meeting if she would like to speak. Ms. Curran said she was there to learn about the possible opportunity with these funds that could help support their efforts to address the conditions at these properties where they have an interest. Chairperson McGiverin thanked Ms. Curran for coming to the meeting and appreciates their efforts to address the situation.

## 6. Adjournment

With no further business, a motion was made by Carl Eger and seconded by Catherine Pratt to adjourn the meeting. A roll call followed:

|---|---|

| Catherine Pratt | Y |
| Michael Sullivan | Y |
